page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-32GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It features 4 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between memory capacity and processing throughput. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core stress-ng performance in the bottom 10% and weak multi-core performance in the bottom 25%. However, memory-centric benchmarks show average performance, with cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 411.23 GB/sec. Large-block uncached read and write operations are weaker, registering at 27.8 GB/sec and 19.94 GB/sec respectively. Geekbench scores sit in the average tier for single-core and multi-core workloads, with text processing showing strong performance in the top 25%.

This server offers high memory density relative to its processing power, presenting a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for memory-bound workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. Tradeoffs include poor static web serving throughput of 2.52 GB/sec and weak Redis SET performance. Large language model inference is limited, with poor performance on 7B models. This profile is suitable for memory-intensive but CPU-light workloads, such as text processing, caching layers, and moderate database operations.
